title: Intel Stock (INTC) Falls 28.6% After Q4 Forecast Miss (Oct 30)
summary: Intel stock (INTC) closed at $65.76 on Oct 30, down 28.58%, after a Q4 forecast below estimates and a warning the PC slowdown will last into next year.
body_markdown:
## Why Intel Stock Fell


According to[Intel's third-quarter release](https://www.intc.com/news-events/press-releases/detail/1786/intel-reports-third-quarter-2026-financial-results) , published at 4:01 p.m. EDT on October 29, 2026, the company forecast fourth-quarter revenue of $15.0 billion to $16.0 billion, non-GAAP gross margin of 38.0% and non-GAAP EPS of $0.25. As reported by[IBTimes](https://www.ibtimes.com.au/intel-shares-plunge-weak-pc-outlook-forecast-1877636) , that revenue range fell short of the roughly $17 billion Wall Street expected, and the EPS guidance came in far below the 43-cent consensus.


The outlook overshadowed the rest of the[earnings report](https://www.heygotrade.com/en/learn/how-to-read-an-earnings-report/) . Third-quarter revenue rose 21% to $16.5 billion, non-GAAP EPS was $0.52 and data center (DCAI) revenue climbed 78% to $7.3 billion, while client revenue fell 5% to $8.1 billion. "Revenue, gross margin and earnings per share exceeded guidance," CFO David Zinsner said in the release, before adding: "we see the PC slowdown continuing at least through the first half of next year."


Per IBTimes, Intel now expects the PC market to shrink 12% in 2026 and another 10% in 2027 as a global memory chip shortage pushes up PC prices. CEO Lip-Bu Tan said those conditions would last "until memory availability and prices begin to normalize." The outlet also reported that an accident in early October forced an extended shutdown at Intel's factory in Israel, which is expected to cut fourth-quarter revenue by about $300 million.


## INTC Stock Analysis: Supporting Factors and Risks


### Supporting Factors


- Data center revenue grew 78% to $7.3 billion in the third quarter, which Zinsner described as "our strongest data center revenue growth in 15 years."
- Intel Foundry revenue rose 58% to $6.7 billion, and Tan said "demand for our CPUs remains robust" despite PC headwinds, a company view.
- According to the[Motley Fool](https://finance.yahoo.com/markets/stocks/articles/prediction-intels-stock-price-end-022000943.html) , Intel's Arizona fab entered high-volume manufacturing in July on a subset of Core Ultra Series 3 "Panther Lake" chips, the first built on Intel 18A.


### Risks


- Intel guided fourth-quarter non-GAAP gross margin to 38.0%, down from 44.1% in the third quarter, and non-GAAP EPS to $0.25, down from $0.52.
- The client business, where revenue already fell 5%, faces a PC slowdown that Zinsner expects to last at least through the first half of next year.
- Intel completed a $23 billion public equity offering in the quarter, per the release, and the Motley Fool notes that new shares split future profits across more holders.
